name: Mercado do Bolhão
short: A neoclassical two-storey market of 1914, fully restored and reopened on 15 September 2022.
long: Mercado do Bolhão is Porto’s best-known market: a monumental neoclassical building of 1914 designed by the architect Correia da Silva. Traders work on two levels, and four entrances sit at different heights between Rua Formosa, Rua de Sá da Bandeira, Rua Alexandre Braga and Rua Fernandes Tomás. After four years of restoration the market reopened on 15 September 2022.
history:
The market’s origins go back to 1839, when the city council decided to create a market square on land bought from the chapter. Here lay a broad meadow crossed by a stream that formed a “bolha” — a bubble of water — which gave the market its name. The square was later improved with access ramps and wooden stalls along the central aisle.

At the start of the 20th century, as the city needed new food supplies, a preliminary project appeared in 1910 by the architect Casimiro Barbosa: a building with two wings on an axis along Rua de Sá da Bandeira. It was abandoned for economic reasons, and in 1914 the present building was erected to a design by the architect Correia da Silva. It was an avant-garde work for its time, combining reinforced concrete with metal structures, timber roofs and granite stonework. In the 1940s an intermediate floor was added, linking the entrances on Rua Alexandre Braga and Rua de Sá da Bandeira.

The market was conceived on a monumental scale: four main entrances at different levels. The south entrance, from Rua Formosa, leads to the lower floor; the side entrances from Rua de Sá da Bandeira and Rua Alexandre Braga lead to an intermediate landing with stairs between floors; the north entrance from Rua Fernandes Tomás opens directly onto the upper floor. Sellers are divided into sections: fish, butchers, vegetables and flowers; around the outside are shops for clothing, cafés, perfumery and fabrics.

On 22 February 2006 the building was listed as a property of public interest, and in 2013 as a monument of public interest. A deep rehabilitation was discussed from the mid-1980s; an international competition in the 1990s was won by a project by the architect Joaquim Massena, but the work never began. In 2007 the market nearly passed to a private developer for 70 years with almost the whole interior demolished — more than 50,000 signatures were gathered against it.

In the end the council carried out the restoration itself: work began in 2018 and lasted more than four years. The market reopened on 15 September 2022. It now has 81 indoor stalls, 10 restaurants and 38 street-facing shops, 12 lifts, a direct metro link and an underground logistics area; 30,000 cubic metres of earth were removed, the façade covers more than 8,000 square metres and the roof more than 5,000.
facts: Built in 1914 to a design by the architect Correia da Silva.
Casimiro Barbosa’s first project (1910) was rejected on cost grounds.
The name comes from a “bolha”, a bubble of water in the stream that ran where the market now stands.
Four entrances at different levels: from Rua Formosa, Rua de Sá da Bandeira, Rua Alexandre Braga and Rua Fernandes Tomás.
Listed as a property of public interest on 22 February 2006.
Reopened on 15 September 2022 after more than four years of restoration.
Today it has 81 stalls, 10 restaurants and 38 street shops, 12 lifts and a direct metro link.
tip: Come before noon for fresh fish and vegetables. The Bolhão metro station is right by the market. Look into the old shops around it: Casa Chineza, Pérola do Bolhão, Casa Transmontana. The upper floor is easiest to reach from Rua Fernandes Tomás.
